description: For each rating, divide the average rental rate by the average rental duration.

c.request: For each film rating, look at its average film length (ignoring films with no length) and its rental rate per day of rental. Which ratings have a per-day rate above the simple mean of the ratings' per-day rates, with each rating counting once? For just those ratings, give one row with their average length, their average per-day rate, and the average amount by which they exceed that mean. Don't round anything. For each rating, divide the average rental rate by the average rental duration.
c.sql:
WITH rating_rates AS (
  SELECT
    rating,
    AVG(length) AS average_length,
    AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day_rate
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
mean_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(per_day_rate) AS simple_mean_rate
  FROM rating_rates
)
SELECT
  rr.rating,
  rr.average_length,
  rr.per_day_rate,
  rr.per_day_rate - mr.simple_mean_rate AS amount_above_mean
FROM rating_rates AS rr
CROSS JOIN mean_rate AS mr
WHERE rr.per_day_rate > mr.simple_mean_rate

a.request: For each film rating, find the average film `length` (ignoring films with no length) and the per-day rental price, defined as the rating's average `rental_rate` divided by its average `rental_duration`. Then take the simple mean of those per-day prices across the ratings, with each rating counting once, and keep only the ratings whose per-day price is above that mean. For those ratings, give one row with the average of their average lengths, the average of their per-day prices, and the average amount by which their per-day price exceeds the cross-rating mean. Don't round anything.
a.sql:
WITH rating_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    rating,
    AVG(length) AS avg_length,
    AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day_price
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
with_mean AS (
  SELECT
    avg_length,
    per_day_price,
    AVG(per_day_price) OVER () AS mean_per_day_price
  FROM rating_metrics
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_length) AS avg_of_avg_lengths,
  AVG(per_day_price) AS avg_per_day_price,
  AVG(per_day_price - mean_per_day_price) AS avg_excess_over_mean
FROM with_mean
WHERE per_day_price > mean_per_day_price;

b.request: For each film rating, calculate average film length from films with a non-null length and calculate the per-day rate as average rental rate divided by average rental duration; select ratings whose per-day rate exceeds the unweighted mean of the per-day rates across ratings, then return each selected rating’s average length, per-day rate, and excess over that mean, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH rating_metrics AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(length) AS avg_length,
         AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day_rate
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
mean_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(per_day_rate) AS mean_per_day_rate
  FROM rating_metrics
)
SELECT rm.rating,
       rm.avg_length,
       rm.per_day_rate,
       rm.per_day_rate - mr.mean_per_day_rate AS excess_over_mean
FROM rating_metrics AS rm
CROSS JOIN mean_rate AS mr
WHERE rm.per_day_rate > mr.mean_per_day_rate;

d.request: For each film rating, divide its average rental rate by its average rental duration. Which ratings have a per-day rate above the simple mean of the ratings’ per-day rates, counting each rating once? For those ratings, give one row with the average film length (ignoring films with no length), the average per-day rate, and the average amount by which each rate exceeds that mean. Don’t round anything.
d.sql:
WITH rating_rates AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day_rate
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
mean_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(per_day_rate) AS mean_per_day_rate
  FROM rating_rates
)
SELECT f.rating,
       AVG(f.length) AS avg_length,
       rr.per_day_rate,
       rr.per_day_rate - mr.mean_per_day_rate AS avg_excess_rate
FROM film f
JOIN rating_rates rr ON rr.rating = f.rating
CROSS JOIN mean_rate mr
WHERE rr.per_day_rate > mr.mean_per_day_rate
GROUP BY f.rating, rr.per_day_rate, mr.mean_per_day_rate;
